title: Contributing to gutenbergr
text: Fork package clone onto computer. haven’t done , recommend using usethis::create_from_github("ropensci/gutenbergr", fork = TRUE). Install development dependencies devtools::install_dev_deps(), make sure package passes R CMD check running devtools::check(). R CMD check doesn’t pass cleanly, ’s good idea ask help continuing. Create Git branch pull request (PR). recommend using usethis::pr_init("brief-description--change"). Make changes, commit git, create PR running usethis::pr_push(), following prompts browser. title PR briefly describe change. body PR contain Fixes #issue-number. user-facing changes, add bullet top NEWS.md (.e. just first header). Follow style described https://style.tidyverse.org/news.html.

text: Project Gutenberg texts processed tibbles lines. analyze book’s progression, ’ll use gutenberg_add_sections(). function identifies headers fills create structural column.
code: persuasion <- persuasion |>   gutenberg_add_sections(     pattern = "^Chapter [IVXLCDM]+",     section_col = "chapter",     format_fn = function(x) {       x |>         str_remove("^CHAPTER\\s+") |>         str_remove("\\.$") |>         as.roman() |>         as.numeric()     }   )  # Preview the new structure persuasion |>   filter(!is.na(chapter)) |>   head() #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   gutenberg_id text                                                title chapter #>          <int> <chr>                                               <chr>   <dbl> #> 1          105 "CHAPTER I."                                        Pers…       1 #> 2          105 ""                                                  Pers…       1 #> 3          105 ""                                                  Pers…       1 #> 4          105 "Sir Walter Elliot, of Kellynch Hall, in Somersets… Pers…       1 #> 5          105 "for his own amusement, never took up any book but… Pers…       1 #> 6          105 "he found occupation for an idle hour, and consola… Pers…       1

title: Text Mining with gutenbergr and tidytext
text: need move one-row-per-line format one-row-per-token format. ’ll use tidytext::unnest_tokens() split text individual words remove stop words tidytext::stop_words.
code: words <- persuasion |>   unnest_tokens(word, text) |>   anti_join(stop_words, by = "word")

title: Text Mining with gutenbergr and tidytext
text: Tokenization makes trivial find frequent words text: Let’s visualize top 20 words:  Character names (Anne, Captain, Elliot, Wentworth) dominate frequent words, makes sense character-driven novel.
code: word_counts <- words |>   count(word, sort = TRUE)  word_counts #> # A tibble: 5,384 × 2 #>    word          n #>    <chr>     <int> #>  1 anne        447 #>  2 captain     302 #>  3 elliot      254 #>  4 lady        214 #>  5 wentworth   191 #>  6 charles     155 #>  7 time        152 #>  8 sir         149 #>  9 miss        125 #> 10 walter      123 #> # ℹ 5,374 more rows word_counts |>   slice_max(n, n = 20) |>   mutate(word = reorder(word, n)) |>   ggplot(aes(x = n, y = word, fill = word)) +   geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(     title = expression(paste("Most Common Words in ", italic("Persuasion"))),     x = "Frequency",     y = NULL   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: Text Mining with gutenbergr and tidytext
text: Let’s use NRC sentiment lexicon, classifies words categories like “joy”, “trust”, “fear”, “sadness”. allow us view overall sentiment book. Note: NRC lexicon requires accepting license agreement installation free non-commercial use. code shows analysis workflow, pre-computed results displayed. Visualize distribution sentiments:
code: nrc_sentiments <- get_sentiments("nrc")  word_sentiments <- words |>   inner_join(nrc_sentiments, by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>   count(sentiment, sort = TRUE) word_sentiments |>   mutate(sentiment = reorder(sentiment, n)) |>   ggplot(aes(x = n, y = sentiment, fill = sentiment)) +   geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(     title = expression(paste(       "Sentiment Distribution in ",       italic("Persuasion")     )),     x = "Word Count",     y = NULL   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: Text Mining with gutenbergr and tidytext
text: can aggregate sentiments chapter structure created earlier.
code: nrc_by_chapter <- words |>   inner_join(nrc_sentiments, by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>   count(chapter, sentiment) |>   filter(!is.na(chapter))  nrc_by_chapter |>   filter(sentiment %in% c("joy", "sadness", "anger", "fear")) |>   ggplot(aes(x = chapter, y = n, fill = factor(sentiment))) +   geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +   facet_wrap(~sentiment, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +   labs(     title = expression(paste("Sentiment by Chapter in ", italic("Persuasion"))),     x = "Chapter",     y = "Word Count"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),     strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")   )

title: Text Mining with gutenbergr and tidytext
text: can also see general emotive content book progresses dividing text bins words track specific emotions fluctuate across narrative arc. good measure, let’s add another x-axis chapter labels can correlate sentiment portions narrative.
code: # Add a running index to preserve order and calculate bins words_with_index <- words |>   mutate(word_index = row_number()) |>   mutate(bin = (word_index - 1) %/% 500 + 1)  nrc_binned <- words_with_index |>   inner_join(nrc_sentiments, by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>   count(bin, sentiment)  # Add labels for chapters chapter_breaks <- words |>   filter(!is.na(chapter)) |>   mutate(word_index = row_number()) |>   group_by(chapter) |>   slice_min(word_index, n = 1) |>   ungroup() |>   mutate(     bin = (word_index - 1) %/% 500 + 1   ) |>   filter(chapter %% 2 == 0)  nrc_binned |>   filter(sentiment %in% c("joy", "sadness", "anger", "fear")) |>   ggplot(aes(x = bin, y = n, color = sentiment)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1, show.legend = FALSE) +   facet_wrap(~sentiment, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +   scale_x_continuous(     name = "Word Bin (500 words)",     sec.axis = sec_axis(       ~.,       breaks = chapter_breaks$bin,       labels = chapter_breaks$chapter,       name = "Chapter"     )   ) +   labs(     title = expression(paste(       "Sentiment Progression in ",       italic("Persuasion")     )),     subtitle = "NRC sentiments by word bin with chapter reference",     y = "Word Count"   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: Text Mining with gutenbergr and tidytext
text: simple frequency tells us main characters , TF-IDF, term frequency–inverse document frequency, tells us words important specific chapter relative rest corpus. excellent identifying specific plot points settings (like move Bath trip Lyme). Highest TF-IDF words chapters 10–13, showing chapter-distinctive terms relative rest novel.
code: chapter_words <- persuasion |>   unnest_tokens(word, text) |>   count(chapter, word, sort = TRUE) |>   bind_tf_idf(word, chapter, n)  # Look at the most "important" words for chapters 10 through 13 chapter_words |>   filter(chapter %in% 10:13) |>   group_by(chapter) |>   slice_max(tf_idf, n = 5) |>   ungroup() |>   mutate(word = reorder(word, tf_idf)) |>   ggplot(aes(tf_idf, word, fill = factor(chapter))) +   geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +   facet_wrap(~chapter, scales = "free") +   labs(     title = "Highest TF-IDF words in Chapters 10-13",     x = "TF-IDF",     y = NULL   ) +   theme_minimal()

what: Common Section Patterns for Project Gutenberg Books
title: Add a section column to a Gutenberg tibble — gutenberg_add_sections
text: Different books use different formatting section markers. patterns common formats: Chapters Roman numerals: "^Chapter [IVXLCDM]+" Chapters Arabic numerals: "^Chapter [0-9]+" Plays Roman Arabic numerals: "^(ACT|SCENE) [IVXLCDM0-9]+" Books (e.g., Paradise Lost): "^BOOK [IVXLCDM]+" Cantos (e.g., Dante's Inferno): "^CANTO [IVXLCDM]+" Staves (e.g., Christmas Carol): "^STAVE [IVXLCDM]+" Multiple formats (e.g., Frankenstein): "^(Letter|Chapter) [0-9]+" Use gutenberg_works() search books examine lines gutenberg_download() determine exact format writing pattern.

title: Add a section column to a Gutenberg tibble — gutenberg_add_sections
code: if (FALSE) { # interactive() # Dante's "Inferno" - Cantos with Roman numerals inferno <- gutenberg_download(1001) |>   gutenberg_add_sections(pattern = "^CANTO [IVXLCDM]+")  # Mary Shelley's "Frankenstein" # Letters and Chapters with Arabic numerals, normalized to title case frankenstein <- gutenberg_download(84) |>   gutenberg_add_sections(     pattern = "^(Letter|Chapter) [0-9]+",     format_fn = stringr::str_to_title   )  # Classic Brontë sisters' works # Chapters with Roman numerals, with trailing periods removed from section text # Consider using `options(gutenbergr_cache_type = "persistent")` # to prevent redownloading in the future. bronte_sisters <- gutenberg_download(   c(     767,  # "Agnes Grey" by Anne Brontë     768,  # "Wuthering Heights" by Emily Brontë     969,  # "The Tenant of Wildfell Hall" by Anne Brontë     1260, # "Jane Eyre" by Charlotte Brontë     9182, # "Villette" by Charlotte Brontë   ),   meta_fields = c("author", "title") ) |>   gutenberg_add_sections(     pattern = "^\\s*CHAPTER [IVXLCDM]+",     format_fn = function(x) str_remove(x, "\\.$")   )  # Leo Tolstoy's "War and Peace" # Add two custom named columns for hierarchical sections war_and_peace <- gutenberg_download(2600) |>   gutenberg_add_sections(     pattern = "^BOOK [A-Z]+",     section_col = "book"   ) |>  gutenberg_add_sections(    pattern = "^CHAPTER [IVXLCDM]+",    section_col = "chapter"  ) }

title: gutenbergr 0.5.2
text: CRAN release: 2026-06-27 gutenberg_get_all_mirrors() now works readMDTable (>= 0.4.0), returns named list tibbles read_md_table() instead single tibble (@jrdnbradford)

title: gutenbergr 0.5.1
text: CRAN release: 2026-05-02 Fixed issue gutenberg_download() duplicated every line works multiple authors (@fditraglia, #148; @jrdnbradford, #149)

title: gutenbergr 0.5.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-03-15 new gutenberg_add_sections() function available create forward-filled section markers (@jrdnbradford, #138) gutenberg_download() now adds User-Agent string identify Project Gutenberg mirror (@jrdnbradford, #139) Documentation now includes two vignettes detail advanced usage (@jrdnbradford, #142, #143, #144)

title: gutenbergr 0.4.1
text: CRAN release: 2026-01-19 cli messaging improved (@jrdnbradford, #134) gutenbergr now logo (@jrdnbradford, #133) gutenberg_get_all_mirrors() now provides helpful instructional messaging instead erroring https://www.gutenberg.org/MIRRORS.unavailable parsed (@jrdnbradford, #132) gutenberg_get_mirror() now falls back known stable mirror (https://aleph.pglaf.org) gutenberg_mirror option set gutenberg_get_all_mirrors() determine mirror (@jrdnbradford, #132) package startup message now appears interactive() (@jrdnbradford, #128)

title: gutenbergr 0.4.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-01-12 gutenbergr now caches works downloaded gutenberg_download(). saved temporary directory default, can configured persist OS-specific application cache directory across sessions (@jrdnbradford, #112, #123). new family gutenberg_cache_* functions now available. allow users list delete items cache, well update cache type (@jrdnbradford, #112, #123). package index reference pkgdown site now separates functions data type (@jrdnbradford, #114). Jordan Bradford (@jrdnbradford) now primary maintainer package. Thanks taking lead, Jordan! (#95).

title: gutenbergr 0.3.1
text: CRAN release: 2025-12-14 language column gutenberg_languages now properly merged language column (#94). default mirror now determined available mirrors gutenberg_get_all_mirrors(), rather trying clever find local mirror. datasets updated 2025-12-14.

title: gutenbergr 0.3.0
text: CRAN release: 2025-05-29 gutenberg_download() tries .txt version files .zip unavailable (@jrdnbradford, #55, #70). New function gutenberg_get_all_mirrors() retrieves mirror data (@jrdnbradford, #58). package infrastructure updated make package robust maintainable (#60, #64, #69). now verify gutenberg_mirror option URL working Gutenberg mirror (@jrdnbradford, #83). now use base R pipe (|>) code examples, magrittr pipe (%>%) (@jonthegeek, #75). fields (gutenberg_languages$language, gutenberg_metadata$language, gutenberg_metadata$rights) now factors reduce object size.

title: gutenbergr 0.2.0

Added gutenberg_languages dataset one-row-per-language-per-work, substantially speeds gutenberg_works. adds files argument gutenberg_download generally used testing. Made changes work dplyr 1.0.0, removing filter_ distinct_. Fixed links https

title: gutenbergr 0.1.1
text: CRAN release: 2016-05-16 Transferred repo ownership ropenscilabs license changed MIT GPL-2. based realization catalog data licensed GPL, package includes processed version catalog data. (See ). Updated datasets 5/5/2016 added “date_updated” attribute tell last updated Added all_languages only_languages arguments gutenberg_works, allowing fine-grained control languages. (example, “either English French” “English French”) Changed get_gutenberg_mirror use xml2 directly, order handle AppVeyor Removed use data() gutenberg_works, since slows gutenberg_works 2X Various documentation, vignette, README adjustments response rOpenSci feedback. Added AppVeyor Windows continuous integration Added code coverage information codecov.io covr, along tests improve coverage

title: gutenbergr 0.1
text: CRAN release: 2016-05-03 gutenberg_download function, downloading one works Project Gutenberg using Gutenberg IDs Datasets Project Gutenberg metadata: gutenberg_metadata, gutenberg_subjects, gutenberg_authors gutenberg_works function retrieve filtered version gutenberg_metadata Introductory vignette including basic examples downloading books Unit tests gutenberg_download gutenberg_works Added NEWS.md file track changes package.
